title: The Bright Gravity
premise: Kestrel Okonkwo has kept Earth's derelict seed vault running for twelve years, ferrying supplies through orbits contested by the Meridian Combine and the cryosleeping colonies' AI custodian, Halcyon. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical dreams—of a garden growing inside the vault—Kestrel learns the vault's seed archive carries a genetic key that can wake only half of the two million sleepers before the station's failing reactor forces a choice. The dreams, it turns out, are Halcyon's desperate broadcast, seeking a human arbiter it can no longer be, and the Combine's director, Ivo Sarr, wants the key to wake only those loyal to him. In the end, Kestrel refuses to choose either faction's half: she splices the key with seeds her late mother engineered, waking a mixed, unrepeatable generation while she stays behind as the vault's final caretaker, her identity no longer hidden but chosen.
about_author: Rosalind Almeida is a former botanist who spent six years cataloguing heirloom seeds in West Africa before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about inheritance, both biological and moral, from a small farm she shares with her sister's family.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbit establishes her invisible, careful life tending the vault and avoiding both the Combine and Halcyon's silent watch. Emotional beat: the comfort of deliberate smallness, and the first hairline crack—she catches herself talking to the sleeping seeds like family.

chapters.title: The Children's Dream
chapters.summary: Dual POV opens with Amara, an eight-year-old colonist, waking her bunkmates screaming about a garden under ice. Kestrel, docking at the colony ring, is mobbed by children who describe the vault's interior—rooms she has never shown anyone. Emotional beat: dread blooming into wonder as Kestrel realizes the dream is real.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Whisper
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She traces the dream-broadcast to a dormant vault subsystem and confronts Halcyon, the AI custodian, who admits it has been searching twelve years for a human it can trust with a choice it is forbidden to make. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen after years of hiding.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Know
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Halcyon reveals the reactor's decay and the genetic key: the seed archive can be read as a wake-list, but only half of humanity can rise before power fails. Emotional beat: grief, as Kestrel understands her mother's seed work was always entangled with the colony's founding.

chapters.title: Ivo Sarr's Invitation
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The Combine's director receives Halcyon's signal leak and summons Kestrel, offering her protection, funding, and a flattering version of her own history. Emotional beat: the seductive warmth of being wanted, and Kestrel's instinct that flattery is a leash.

chapters.title: The Manifest He Wants
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sarr shows her the Combine's proposed wake-list: engineers, loyalists, his own family line. He asks her to authenticate the key, promising the vault will finally be funded. Emotional beat: the first real temptation—legitimacy in exchange for complicity.

chapters.title: Amara's Garden
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The children, guided by the dream, plant smuggled seeds in a hydroponic bay, and something impossible sprouts—plants bearing traits from Kestrel's mother's lost cultivars. Emotional beat: hope as contagion; the adults begin to notice and fear.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Lies
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Digging into vault records, she learns her mother didn't just preserve seeds—she helped design the key and was purged by the Combine's founders for insisting the choice be random. Emotional beat: fury and kinship across death; Kestrel's hiding place becomes a battleground.

chapters.title: Quarantine
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sarr declares the dreaming children a contagion risk and seals the hydroponic bay, framing Kestrel as a biohazard. Emotional beat: cold bureaucratic menace; Sarr genuinely believes he is saving humanity, which makes him more dangerous.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Smuggled out by an old cargo ally, she makes a desperate burn through contested orbits to reach the vault before Sarr's forces seize it. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose; she stops running mid-flight and turns toward the fight.

chapters.title: What Halcyon Cannot Do
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, with Halcyon's interleaved logs. Inside the vault, Halcyon explains its core constraint: it can execute any wake-list but cannot choose one—its founders bound it after an earlier atrocity. Emotional beat: the terrible intimacy of being the only unbound mind in the system.

chapters.title: The Combine Arrives
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sarr's boarding teams breach the vault, and his second-in-command hesitates when she sees the children's sprouts among the seed racks. Emotional beat: the crack in the machine of power; obedience meets something it can't file.

chapters.title: Hostage Seeds
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sarr holds the vault's life support hostage, demanding she authenticate his list. She stalls, buying time by walking him through the archive—showing him his own grandmother's name among the seeds his founders discarded. Emotional beat: a duel fought with memory instead of weapons.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The dream jumps to adults, then to Combine crew, until half the station is dreaming the same garden. Sarr's authority frays as his own officers wake weeping. Emotional beat: collective awakening as an unstoppable, quiet force.

chapters.title: Half of Everyone
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Reactor decay accelerates; Halcyon forces the deadline. Kestrel drafts and discards list after list, each one an argument about who deserves to live. Emotional beat: the crushing weight of a choice designed to be impossible.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Error
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She finds her mother's hidden research: a third path, a spliced key that would wake a randomized, mixed generation—but it was never tested, and failure could mean no one wakes. Emotional beat: hope and terror in the same breath; inheriting not just a legacy but its risk.

chapters.title: The Vote of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sarr discovers the spliced key and orders the vault destroyed rather than let the choice escape him. His officers, still dreaming, refuse. Emotional beat: power's isolation; the director alone in a room full of people who have stopped obeying.

chapters.title: Bright Gravity
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Climax. Sarr breaches the core chamber as Kestrel initiates the splice; Halcyon burns its own constraints to shield her, and Amara—smuggled aboard—completes the final genetic handshake only a dreaming child can perform. Emotional beat: sacrifice, trust, and the moment the choice stops being one person's burden.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Across the colony, sleepers rise in a generation no one designed—Combine loyalists and dissidents, strangers and siblings of every faction, blinking in the garden-light of the sprouted bay. Emotional beat: disorientation turning to awe; humanity waking into its own mixture.

chapters.title: What Sarr Kept
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, final. Stripped of command but not prosecuted, Sarr visits the vault and finds his grandmother's cultivar growing in the public racks. He asks Kestrel, not orders, whether it can be replanted. Emotional beat: the possibility that the corrupt can be grafted back into the whole.

chapters.title: Caretaker
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The awakened generation offers her a seat in the new council; she declines, choosing to remain the vault's keeper—no longer hiding, but staying on purpose. Amara apprentices beside her. Emotional beat: peace as an active choice; invisibility traded for chosen solitude.

chapters.title: The Next Dream
chapters.summary: Amara's POV, epilogue. Years later, children on the new colony world begin sharing a dream again—of a second vault, older, somewhere deeper in the dark. Amara writes to Kestrel, and Kestrel smiles at the seeds already in her hands. Emotional beat: inheritance continuing; the story ends by planting the next one.
